full_judgment:
2. Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Additional Sessions Judge acted illegally in passing the impugned order allowing the revision and setting aside the order dated 3-4-83 passed by the learned Additional District Magistrate in CR Case No. 346 of 1974 inasmuch as a second revision is not maintainable and that the same was barred by limitation. 

 6. Learned Advocate for the petitioners relied, in support of his contention that the revision in question filed before the Sessions Judge long after 30 days was barred by limitation. in the case of Md. Nur Ali vs. State reported in 12 DLR 681. Justice Rahman, as his Lordship then was, sitting singly, held that period of limitation to move the Sessions Judge by way of revision was 30 days from the order complained of by analogy with the period of limitation provided for filing of appeals. But his Lordship did not interfere with the order of the Sessions Judge who entertained the revisional application beyond the period of limitation as he found on consideration of merit of the case that the Sessions Judge had done substantial justice. In the instant case also learned Additional Sessions Judge found that the learned Additional District Magistrate acted illegally in passing the order dated 3-4-83 acquitting the accused persons without trial though both the parties were present in Court and on consideration of facts which were found to be incorrect by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. In the facts and circumstances of the case the impugned order passed by the learned Additional Sessions Judge does not require any interference from this Court on merit as we find that illegality committed by the learned Additional District Magistrate was set aside by the learned Additional Sessions Judge. Learned Advocate for the petitioners did not argue on the question of merit of the impugned order. So his contention as to limitation in the facts and circumstances of the case does not appeal to us. In the above facts and circumstances we are of the view that a revisional application filed beyond the period of limitation though should not be encouraged, cannot debar the Court from setting aside an illegal order of the subordinate Court in the interest of justice.
